subject: Closing cadence & seqlen scaling: KV-cache impact on TTFT and concurrency
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tellis@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff: long-context perf requirements and timeline

Evelyn / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We need to lock a mutual action plan and the benchmarking scope so procurement can greenlight a pilot. Key asks from our side:
- Validate TTFT (time to first token) for sequences up to ~65k tokens using our prompt mixes.
- Report p50/p95 token latency and end-to-end throughput at 1/5/10/50 concurrent streams.
- Show KV-cache impact: cold vs warmed cache, and cache hit rate sensitivity when prompt prefix distributions vary.

We have a narrow close window (end of Q3). Can you map out a test plan, expected deliverables, and a close timeline we can put into our MAP? I can share a representative prompt set if useful.

Thanks,
Tom
Head of AI Engineering
Acme Robotics

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tellis@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Lina Park <lina.park@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: long-context perf requirements and timeline

Tom — appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a draft MAP timeline (MAP-timeline.pdf) and the test matrix CSV (kvcache-sweep-plan.csv). High-level plan below; we can iterate after you share the prompt set.

Planned benchmark deliverables (week-by-week during pilot):
- Week 0: onboarding + prompt ingestion and small sanity runs.
- Week 1: SeqLen sweep: 8k / 16k / 32k / 48k / 65k tokens — measure TTFT, p50/p95 per-token latency, and peak throughput at single stream.
- Week 2: Concurrency sweep: 1 / 5 / 10 / 50 concurrent streams at selected seq lengths, include cold and warm KV-cache runs.
- Week 3: Prompt-distribution stress: skewed prefixes (70% repeat), uniform random, and long-tail tails — measure cache hit % and degradation.
- Week 4: Regression checks, final report, and runbook (inc. recommended batch sizes, quantization profile, and fallback SLOs).

Key measurement definitions:
- TTFT: wall-clock time from request accept to first token emitted (server side).
- Per-token latency: measured on a per-token basis after streaming begins (report p50/p95).
- Throughput: completed tokens/sec aggregated across streams.
- KV-cache warm= >95% prefix reuse; cold=first-run after model load.

Proposed MAP milestones / close cadence:
- 2027-07-05: Confirm prompt set + signature on pilot statement of work.
- 2027-07-12: Start pilot runs (Week 0 onboarding).
- 2027-08-09: Pilot completion + delivery of final report.
- 2027-08-16: Executive review and commercial decision (aim to close by EOM Aug, latest Sep 15).

Attachments: MAP-timeline.pdf (timeline + responsibilities), kvcache-sweep-plan.csv (detailed test matrix).

If this looks good I’ll schedule a 30m kickoff with Karthik and Jonas to agree infra specs and resource commitments.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Principal GTM Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tellis@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Lina Park <lina.park@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: long-context perf requirements and timeline

Looping in a few technical notes so we set expectations up front. Quoting Evelyn's plan below for context.

> Planned benchmark deliverables (week-by-week during pilot):
> - Week 1: SeqLen sweep: 8k / 16k / 32k / 48k / 65k tokens ...

A couple of practical constraints and additions from infra:
- Max practical seqlen on our verified stack today is 65k — tests at 65k will run on a tuned config (larger KV segments, different attention kernels). Expect higher memory pressure; we’ll run a capacity check before the full sweep.
- Please include a "gravity" run at realistic prompt-size distribution (see note below) — synthetic fixed-length tests are useful but not dispositive.
- KV-cache warmup methodology: run N warmup requests that include the top 200 prefixes; track cache occupancy and effective hit-rate. We recommend N=250 warmup requests per configuration. We will include both TTL and LRU eviction simulations.
- Add an explicit "prefix fragmentation" test: simulate when prefixes vary across 30% of requests to stress cache miss patterns.

Data to capture in each run (CSV rows): seq_len, prompt_type, cache_state (cold/warm), p50_TTFT_ms, p95_TTFT_ms, tokens_per_sec, cpu_util, gpu_mem_gb, cache_hit_pct, wall_time_s. We’ve added this schema to kvcache-sweep-plan.csv.

I’ll prepare a dry-run on Redwood Dedicated infra (controlled capacity) the week prior to pilot and share kvcache-sweep-results.csv after the first concurrency sweep.

—Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tellis@acme.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lina Park <lina.park@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: long-context perf requirements and timeline

Tom — quick commercial note: we can include a 2-week pilot credit (covers infra runs) tied to the MAP signature. If we see throughput degradation at 65k we’ll surface optimization levers: quantization variant, reduced KV segment sizes, and routing to a lower-latency model variant for short requests.

If procurement needs a specific SLO ask for the pilot, propose: TTFT p95 <= 1.2s for <=8k, <=2.8s for 32k, and a best-effort target for 65k (we’ll capture exact numbers in the report). That maps to a conservative commercial commitment while we validate production numbers.

Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Ellis <tellis@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: long-context perf requirements and timeline

Thanks — that proposed cadence looks actionable. Two quick asks before kickoff:
1) Please add one additional high-stress run at 90k tokens to demonstrate failure modes and fallback behavior — we understand it’s beyond the verified stack but need to document limits. If 90k is impossible, please capture the max stable seq_len and the failure signature (OOM vs swap vs graceful degrade).
2) Include explicit fallback workflows in the runbook: model variant routing, token truncation heuristics, and KV suffix compaction.

We’ll sign the pilot SOW after an internal exec sync next Wed (07/07). I’ll share the prompt set by COB Monday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Tom
Head of AI Engineering
Acme Robotics
